pack.title: First dates
pack.description: Tests disguised as small talk. Answer the question, keep your dignity.

scenarios.setting: First date, drinks. Midway through your story, they check their watch.
scenarios.jab: So anyway — how much do you make, roughly?

replies.line: Enough to buy my own drinks. Next question.
replies.why: It answers the spirit of the question while keeping the number private forever.
It labels the timing as the problem, which lets the date continue cleanly.

replies.line: Ha — ask me on date three. What do you do when you're not auditing strangers?
replies.why: Humor plus a redirect keeps the night alive without opening your books.

replies.line: Somewhere between intern and Bond villain. You?
replies.why: A joke answer to an audit question signals the topic is closed and the night isn't.

replies.line: Salary talk? Buy me dinner first.
replies.why: It prices the question as intimacy, which either charms them or ends the audit.

trap.why: Walking out over one clumsy question spends a whole evening to win a moment.

scenarios.setting: First date. They've spent twenty minutes on their ex.
scenarios.jab: Sorry, sorry — my ex just really messed me up, you know?

replies.line: I hear you. Tonight I'm getting to know you, not them.
replies.why: It shows empathy while drawing the evening's boundary in one calm line.

replies.line: Fresh start tonight. Tell me something good.
replies.why: It grants the past one nod, then physically steers the night forward.

replies.line: That sounds rough — I hope tonight can be a lighter chapter.
replies.why: Kindness about the hurt plus a gentle bid for the present keeps both intact.

replies.line: At this rate I should've brought them flowers too.
replies.why: It points out the third wheel at the table with a joke instead of a complaint.

replies.line: Should I save you the middle seat?
replies.why: Treating the ex as a third date reframes the monologue as a seating problem.

scenarios.setting: End of a decent first date. They walk you to your car.

replies.line: Mine's not on the table tonight. I had a good time.
replies.why: A clear no plus genuine warmth leaves no ambiguity and no insult.
replies.delivery: Say it smiling, then keep walking. Don't negotiate.

replies.why: It declines completely in four words, with the good night doing the kindness.

replies.line: I don't move that fast — but I'd like a second date.
replies.why: It frames the no as your pace, not their failure, and offers the future explicitly.

replies.line: My place has a strict guest list. Me.
replies.why: Absurd bureaucracy makes the no final without making the night cold.
It grades the ask while keeping the verdict to one syllable.

trap.line: Ugh, I knew this was all you wanted.
trap.why: Assuming the worst about the whole date burns someone who took one shot.
